title: CT doll said to be inhabited by an 'inhuman spirit' brought to new site. You can see her and she's not alone.
excerpt: There are various ways to view the collection, including a flashlight experience, paranormal investigation and more.
content:
The contents of a famous Occult Museum founded by late paranormal investigators Ed and Lorraine Warren are now on display in Salem, Massachusetts at The Haunted Warren Museum, including Annabelle, dubbed the scariest doll in the world.

The display will be there until Christmas, according to the website.

The collection is now owned by superstar comedian Matt Rife and his friend, YouTuber Elton Castee.

Fans of the paranormal are so convinced of Annabelle’s evil powers, they expressed fear for Rife’s safety when the acquisition was announced. Then rumors swirled about Annabelle when her handler died unexpectedly during a tour – Annabelle doesn’t like to be moved – but it was later revealed he died of an event that was caused by underlying disease.

The museum contents and different modes of viewing it will be on display at 259 Essex Street, Salem, Mass., according to a Facebook post.

For more information, contact info@hauntedwarrenmuseum.com.

“For the first time in history, the legendary collection of Ed & Lorraine Warren’s Occult Museum has found a public home—giving you the unprecedented opportunity to stand face-to-face with some of the world’s most infamous paranormal artifacts,” the Facebook post states.

“Encounter the real Annabelle and explore more than 1,000 authentic haunted objects, cursed artifacts, occult relics, true crime evidence, and historical treasures from around the world.”

The artifacts are from legendary paranormal cases, some of which led to iconic movies, including including Amityville, The Conjuring House, The Devil Made Me Do It, and more.

The museum existed for many years on the Warrens’ property in Monroe, Conn. but was rarely open to the public. Happenings of events that occurred inside the museum became legend.

There are various ways to view the collection, including a flashlight experience, paranormal investigation and more.

“For the first time in history, you can explore it on your own,” the Facebook post says.
Admission starts at $49.99.

The Facebook post asks, “Do you have what it takes to conquer your fears?”

Annabelle, a classic-looking Raggedy Ann doll acquired during an investigation by Warrens that is said to be “inhabited by an “inhuman spirit.”

She’s been known to attack when angered or make bad things happen to people, according to reports.

The doll got so rambunctious during the ride to the Warren’s home in Monroe from an investigation site, that Ed Warren had to sprinkle her with holy water to continue. Recently, her handler, Dan Rivera died mysteriously on tour with Annabelle and once a museum visitor who taunted her died in a crash after leaving.

One fan wrote to Rife on Facebook, “Just remember not to joke around with Annabelle and the rest of the museum.”

Someone else begged him to “get rid of it.”

“It is far too sinister and we need you around – you make us all laugh!” she wrote.

Rife announced in a TikTok video when he purchased the collection that he and Castee were going to allow overnights in the terrifying place as a thrill to paranormal community.

Rife, who often brings the paranormal into his comedy, has said on Facebook he “couldn’t be happier to own such prominent piece of paranormal history!”

“I can’t wait to operate this place with the respect and care it deserves, whilst becoming the greatest paranormal investigation location in the country.”

The real Annabelle doll is an innocent-looking old-fashioned Raggedy Ann doll. The doll used in the Annabelle movies is a frightening-looking porcelain doll.

The Warrens took control of Annabelle during an investigation in the 1970s after a young Hartford nurse received the doll as a gift from her mother and numerous creepy things occurred.

Later, the nurse claimed the doll attacked her friend. She held a séance and was told the doll held the ghost of a girl named Annabelle. The nurse called a priest. The priest told her to call the Warrens.

The Warrens decided “there was something evil in that doll,” their son-in-law Tony Spera has said.

The nurse called the priest to do an exorcism on the house and bless the nurse and her roommate.

It all started when, “One day the nurse came home and thought, I could have sworn I put that doll on the couch. It was in the bedroom. Then it happened more,” Spera has said. “One day she was sitting at the breakfast nook with the doll and suddenly the doll’s arms moved.”

The Warrens are also famous for their investigation of a haunted house in Amityville, NY, and the 1980s Connecticut poltergeist case based on a Warren case, in which demonic possession was used unsuccessfully as a defense in a murder trial.

The late Lorraine Warren has said the power of her Catholic faith has gotten her out of frightening situations because she uses goodness to fight the demonic. Holy water was a frequent tool used.

Other highlights of the museum include Ouija boards, Voodoo dolls, objects used in satanic rituals, a coffin that a 17-year-old boy allegedly slept in before stalking women at night and artifacts from a plane that crashed into the Florida Everglades, according to Courant archives.
